{{Short description|American mathematician (born 1948)}}
[[File:John R Steel.jpg|thumb|John Steel in 2004]]
'''John Robert Steel''' (born October 30, 1948) is an American [[set theory|set theorist at]] the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (formerly at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]]).  He has made many contributions to the theory of [[inner model]]s and [[determinacy]].  With [[Donald A. Martin]], he proved [[projective determinacy]],<ref name="Projective determinacy">{{cite journal|author=Martin, Donald A. and John R. Steel|date=Jan 1989|title=A Proof of Projective Determinacy|jstor=1990913|journal=Journal of the American Mathematical Society|volume=2|issue=1|pages=71–125|doi=10.2307/1990913|doi-access=free}}</ref> assuming the existence of sufficiently [[large cardinal]]s.  He earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in Logic & the Methodology of Science at Berkeley in 1977 under the joint supervision of John West Addison Jr. and [[Steve Simpson (mathematician)|Stephen G. Simpson]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=22128}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 1988, the Association for Symbolic Logic awarded him, [[Donald A. Martin]], and [[W. Hugh Woodin]] the Karp Prize for their work on the consistency of determinacy relative to large cardinals. In 2015, the European Set Theory Society awarded him and [[Ronald Jensen]] the [[Hausdorff Medal]] for their paper "K without the measurable".

In 2012, Steel held the [[Gödel Lecture]] titled ''The hereditarily ordinal definable sets in models of determinacy.''
